page: Amazon Web Services t3.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 virtual CPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the t3.xlarge in the lower tiers for sustained workloads. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance register in the bottom 25% (weak). Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached and uncached read/write operations, similarly fall into the weak category. For specialized tasks, such as bzip3 decompression, Redis SET operations, and static web serving, performance is measured in the bottom 10% (poor). These results reflect the burstable CPU allocation model, which is designed for variable workloads rather than sustained high-throughput computation.

The burstable resource model offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads with fluctuating demand. By utilizing CPU credits to handle occasional spikes, the instance avoids the higher cost of continuously allocated compute resources. However, sustained utilization beyond the baseline credit accumulation rate results in performance throttling or additional charges. This profile makes the t3.xlarge suitable for low-traffic web servers, small databases, development environments, and code repositories where continuous maximum CPU performance is not required.
